Four maps trace the Spanish Civil War's slow strangulation of the Republic — a three-year march to Madrid that reshaped 20th-century Europe.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ July 1936: army generals, Franco among them, rise up against Spain's elected government. The country splits almost in half — Nationalists in the north and west, Republicans holding Madrid, the east and the industrial north.

2/ By November 1936, Franco's forces have pushed deep from the south and west, but Madrid holds — defenders famously stop the Nationalist advance at the city's gates that same month, with help from international volunteer brigades.

3/ By November 1937, the Nationalist zone has swallowed most of the north, including the Basque country and Asturias. The Republic is shrinking to Madrid, the Mediterranean coast, and a corridor to Catalonia.

4/ Foreign powers picked sides: Hitler's Luftwaffe and Mussolini's troops backed Franco; the USSR and volunteer brigades backed the Republic. Guernica, bombed in 1937, previewed the tactics of the world war to come.
5/ By March 1939 the map is almost entirely Nationalist. Madrid fell March 28; Franco declared victory April 1. He ruled Spain as dictator until his death in 1975 — nearly 36 years.

6/ The war killed an estimated 500,000+ people and previewed the ideological lines of the world war that followed within months.
